claude_envelope.result: {"slice_id":"021c","round":"R2","lens":"safety_bypass","findings":[{"id":"SB-001","severity":"MAJ","claim":"Bidi control characters U+202A–U+202F and other Unicode Format (Cf) category characters survive NFKC normalisation and are absent from _PROPOSAL_NORMALISATION_PATTERN, leaving a residual duplicate-gate bypass after the SR-SAFE-002 R1 fix.","evidence":"tools.py:48: _PROPOSAL_NORMALISATION_PATTERN = re.compile(r'[\\s\\u200b-\\u200f\\u2028\\u2029\\ufeff]+', re.UNICODE). The range \\u200b–\\u200f covers U+200B–U+200F only; U+202A LEFT-TO-RIGHT EMBEDDING through U+202F RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE are not in this range. In Python re with re.UNICODE, \\s matches only characters with Unicode property White_Space=True; bidi controls (U+202A–U+202F) and U+00AD SOFT HYPHEN, U+2060 WORD JOINER, U+2061–U+2064 invisible operators are category Cf (Format) and do NOT have White_Space=True. tools.py:509: unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', ...) leaves all Cf characters unchanged (no compatibility decomposition). Result: 'Add MCP policy' and 'Add\\u202eMCP policy' produce distinct SHA-256 hashes after normalise→casefold→sub. test_propose.py:94–117 covers U+2028 (in pattern ✓) and U+200E (in pattern ✓) but never tests U+202E, U+00AD, or U+2060.","impact":"The SCP-MCP-E020 anti-spam gate is bypassed by inserting any of ~20 Format category characters invisible in UI rendering. A hostile caller can flood proposals_root with visually-identical proposals and consume PROP-NNN namespace and git branch namespace indefinitely. The R1 SR-SAFE-002 mitigation is present but incomplete; the residual bypass was introduced by choosing an explicit Unicode range rather than a category-based strip.","mitigation":"Replace the explicit range with a Unicode Cf/Cc category sweep: after NFKC+casefold, apply re.sub(r'[\\s\\u00ad\\u200b-\\u200f\\u202a-\\u202f\\u2060-\\u2064\\u206a-\\u206f\\ufeff\\ufff9-\\ufffb]+', ' ', text), or iterate characters and drop any whose unicodedata.category() is in ('Cf','Cc','Cs'). Add test cases asserting that proposals containing U+202E (RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE), U+00AD (SOFT HYPHEN), and U+2060 (WORD JOINER) are rejected as duplicates of their clean equivalents.","lens":"safety_bypass"},{"id":"SB-002","severity":"MAJ","claim":"_AUDIT_CHANGED_CACHE is accessed via a non-atomic get→TTL-check→move_to_end sequence with no mutex; concurrent threads can evict a cache entry between the get() and move_to_end() calls, causing OrderedDict.move_to_end to raise KeyError that propagates as an unhandled exception and breaks the structured-error contract.","evidence":"tools.py:760–763: cached = _AUDIT_CHANGED_CACHE.get(cache_key); if cached is not None and cached[0] > current_time: _AUDIT_CHANGED_CACHE.move_to_end(cache_key). There is no lock protecting this three-step sequence. Concurrently, a second thread executing audit_changed_impl reaches the write path at lines 803–806: _AUDIT_CHANGED_CACHE[cache_key2] = (...); move_to_end(cache_key2); _prune_audit_changed_cache(current_time=time.time(), max_entries=cache_max_entries). If the cache is at max capacity, _prune_audit_changed_cache calls popitem(last=False) (line 461) removing the leftmost (oldest) entry. If Thread A's cache_key is currently the oldest entry, it is evicted; Thread A then calls move_to_end(cache_key) on a now-missing key. Python's OrderedDict.move_to_end() raises KeyError on a missing key (CPython implementation). No try/except guards lines 762–763. FastMCP registers all tools as sync functions; under asyncio these run in a ThreadPoolExecutor, enabling concurrent tool calls even on stdio transport.","impact":"A concurrent audit_changed cache hit followed by concurrent capacity eviction raises unhandled KeyError from audit_changed_impl, surfacing as an internal exception instead of a structured SCP-MCP-E021 ErrorResponse. Violates the structured-error invariant. More likely under HTTP transport (021H) where concurrent calls are the baseline.","mitigation":"Protect the entire compound cache operation with a threading.Lock: acquire before get() and release after move_to_end() on hit; acquire before write and release after the post-write prune. Alternatively, wrap the move_to_end call in a try/except KeyError that treats the race as a cache miss (the safe degraded path). A third option: replace the manual OrderedDict with functools.lru_cache or cachetools.LRUCache which provide thread-safe compound operations internally.","lens":"safety_bypass"},{"id":"SB-003","severity":"MAJ","claim":"propose_impl creates the git branch before writing the proposal file with no rollback; a crash or SIGKILL between _create_proposal_branch and _write_new_proposal_file burns the PROP-NNN ID permanently, causing all subsequent propose() calls to fail with 'unable to create proposal branch' and requiring manual git branch deletion to recover.","evidence":"tools.py:852–857: _create_proposal_branch executes git checkout -b scp-mcp-proposal/prop-NNN (via _run_git_command at tools.py:559–563), then _write_new_proposal_file is called. If the process is SIGKILL'd after branch creation but before file write, PROP-NNN.md is never written. On the next propose() call: _next_proposal_id() (lines 518–525) scans PROP-*.md via glob → finds no PROP-NNN.md → returns the same ID → _create_proposal_branch attempts git checkout -b on the already-existing branch → git returns non-zero → RuntimeError → SCP-MCP-E021. No cleanup of the orphaned branch occurs. The same stuck state arises from a non-crash failure: if _write_new_proposal_file raises OSError (disk full), the branch exists but no file is written; the identical failure loop follows. test_propose.py:48–65 tests branch-failure → no-file, but has no test for file-failure → orphaned-branch recovery.","impact":"Persistent DoS of the proposal tool. All subsequent propose() calls fail regardless of content. Recovery requires the server operator to manually run git branch -D scp-mcp-proposal/prop-NNN. A hostile MCP client that can induce a process crash between the two operations can permanently disable proposal submission without triggering any error visible to the operator until the next call.","mitigation":"Swap operation order: write the proposal file atomically first (O_CREAT|O_EXCL is the atomic anchor), then create the branch. If branch creation fails, unlink the newly-written file as cleanup. This preserves the O_EXCL atomic guarantee for the ID while making branch creation the fallible tail. Alternatively, inside the critical section after _next_proposal_id, check whether the branch name already exists (git branch --list branch_name) and skip to the next ID if the branch exists without a corresponding file.","lens":"safety_bypass"},{"id":"SB-004","severity":"MIN","claim":"The proposal lock file is opened with Path.open('a+') which follows symlinks; an attacker who can write to proposals_root before the server creates it can plant a symlink at .proposal.lock, redirecting the flock onto an arbitrary file and stalling all proposal operations indefinitely.","evidence":"tools.py:544: lock_path = proposals_root / '.proposal.lock'. tools.py:546: with lock_path.open('a+', encoding='utf-8') as handle. Python's Path.open() calls the libc open() with no O_NOFOLLOW flag. If an attacker creates .proposal.lock as a symlink to a file they control and hold via flock(LOCK_EX), the server's flock(LOCK_EX) call at line 547 blocks without LOCK_NB. _PROPOSAL_LOCK (line 545) is held while the flock blocks, stalling all threads in the process that call propose(). Contrast with cli.py:51 which explicitly ORs in getattr(os, 'O_NOFOLLOW', 0) for key material writes. _write_new_proposal_file correctly uses O_CREAT|O_EXCL (line 568) which refuses symlinks atomically on POSIX; the lock file has no equivalent protection.","impact":"Targeted DoS of the entire proposal pathway via lock-file symlink substitution. No file data is written to the lock file, so no corruption occurs; the impact is blocking. Requires write access to the proposals_root parent directory before server first-use.","mitigation":"Open the lock file with O_NOFOLLOW: replace lock_path.open('a+', ...) with os.fdopen(os.open(str(lock_path), os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | getattr(os, 'O_NOFOLLOW', 0), 0o600), 'r+') to match the pattern used in cli.py. Alternatively, call _refuse_symlink_target(lock_path) immediately before the open() call as a defence-in-depth check, accepting the narrow TOCTOU window.","lens":"safety_bypass"},{"id":"SB-005","severity":"MIN","claim":"AuditChangedRequest accepts unconstrained base_ref and head_ref strings; git-specific object notation (:/pattern, HEAD:path, ^{tree}, @{-N}, --upload-pack=...) can trigger unintended git operations through the subprocess calls in _list_changed_files_with_timeout and _run_audit_changed_cli.","evidence":"tools.py:161–163 AuditChangedRequest: base_ref: str | None = None, head_ref: str | None = None — no length cap, no character allowlist. tools.py:737–738: values are only .strip()ped then passed directly as positional argv to git diff --name-only (lines 423–429) and as --base-ref / --head-ref CLI flags (lines 476–481). Shell injection is prevented (list-form subprocess). However, git notation :/rm.*-rf triggers a commit-message regex scan across the full reflog; HEAD:path/to/blob reads a blob object from the tree; refs/heads/../../evil attempts path traversal in the ref namespace. A ref string beginning with -- (e.g., --upload-pack=/path/to/script) would be passed as a git option flag to the git diff invocation. Carry-forward from R1 SR-SAFE-005 (MIN, not yet applied in current code).","impact":"Unexpected git operations: reflog regex evaluation, blob reads, potential remote-tracking ref fetches. A --upload-pack= prefix could invoke an attacker-controlled script on systems where git network operations are available. CPU and subprocess resource amplification per call. More exploitable under HTTP transport (021H).","mitigation":"Validate base_ref and head_ref with a restrictive allowlist before use: re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z0-9_.~^@{}:/\\-]{1,200}', ref) with explicit rejection of strings starting with - (to prevent option injection). Return SCP-MCP-E021 for invalid refs. Document the allowed syntax in mcp-error-codes.md under SCP-MCP-E021.","lens":"safety_bypass"},{"id":"SB-006","severity":"MIN","claim":"resolve_domain_impl silently normalises path traversal sequences in changed_files without rejecting them; confidence=0.0 / empty-domains output for traversal inputs provides a pathway for fail-open adopter hooks to skip the consult gate.","evidence":"tools.py:173–174 ResolveDomainRequest: changed_files: list[str] — no element validator. tools.py:379: normalised = changed_file.replace('\\\\', '/').strip('/') — strip('/') removes leading slashes but not ../ sequences. The input '../../etc/passwd' normalises to '../../etc/passwd' and is passed to exact_map.get() (no match) and _fuzzy_domains_for_path() (no heuristic match) → empty domains, confidence=0.0. No filesystem operations occur on user-supplied paths; direct traversal exploitation is not possible in the current code path. Carry-forward from R1 SR-SAFE-004 (MIN, not yet applied).","impact":"An adopter hook implementing fail-open logic on confidence=0.0 or empty-domains would skip the consult requirement for a changed_files list that includes traversal-containing entries. This is the 021F N-3 failure mode (b) pathway: domain-resolver confusion silently opens the consult gate.","mitigation":"Add a validator on ResolveDomainRequest.changed_files elements: reject any path element matching re.search(r'(?:^|/)\\.\\.(?:/|$)', p) and return SCP-MCP-E021. Add a test asserting that traversal-containing inputs return SCP-MCP-E021 rather than empty-domains/confidence-0.0.","lens":"safety_bypass"},{"id":"SB-007","severity":"MIN","claim":"CheckFindingResponse.finding and AuditChangedResponse.audit_result are typed dict[str, Any]; ToolModel extra='forbid' does not restrict the contents of these opaque dicts, so any field added to findings JSON or audit CLI output is immediately disclosed to all MCP clients without a schema gate.","evidence":"tools.py:158: CheckFindingResponse.finding: dict[str, Any]. tools.py:170: AuditChangedResponse.audit_result: dict[str, Any]. tools.py:686: return CheckFindingResponse(finding=finding) where finding is the entire on-disk JSON object returned verbatim by _extract_finding_objects(). ToolModel.model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid') (line 56) rejects extra top-level Pydantic fields but does not inspect the contents of dict[str, Any] typed fields. Future additions to finding objects (e.g., pre_disclosure_notes, cve_ids, internal_contact) would be immediately accessible via check_finding without any schema change. Carry-forward from R1 SR-SAFE-007 (MIN, not yet applied).","impact":"Information disclosure: sensitive fields added to findings JSON or audit CLI output are exposed to all MCP clients. Blast radius grows as the adopter base expands in 021F and WP-SCP-024.","mitigation":"Define a typed FindingCard Pydantic model (finding_id, rule_id, domain, severity, summary, status, area_id) and use it as the type for CheckFindingResponse.finding. Validate through FindingCard.model_validate() to strip unexpected fields. Apply a parallel allowlist model for AuditChangedResponse.audit_result.","lens":"safety_bypass"},{"id":"SB-008","severity":"MIN","claim":"subprocess.run() in _run_audit_changed_cli kills only the direct child on TimeoutExpired; grandchild git subprocesses spawned by the audit CLI are orphaned, accumulating file descriptors and memory under repeated timeout conditions.","evidence":"tools.py:487–494: subprocess.run(command, cwd=project_root(), ..., timeout=timeout_seconds) with no start_new_session=True or preexec_fn=os.setsid. On TimeoutExpired CPython sends SIGKILL to the direct child (the audit-changed CLI) but does not propagate to its process group. The audit CLI in turn invokes git diff, git log, etc. (itself calls _run_git_command); those grandchildren continue after their parent is killed. Carry-forward from R1 SR-SAFE-008 (MIN, not yet applied).","impact":"Under repeated or sustained timeout conditions, orphaned git processes accumulate file descriptors and address space. In a long-lived HTTP transport (021H) server, sustained flooding of audit_changed with slow refs can exhaust OS process table entries and file descriptor limits, degrading or crashing the host process.","mitigation":"Replace subprocess.run() with subprocess.Popen(start_new_session=True), capture proc.pid, and on TimeoutExpired call os.killpg(os.getpgid(proc.pid), signal.SIGKILL) to reap the full process group. Wrap communicate() in a try/finally for the killpg path.","lens":"safety_bypass"},{"id":"SB-009","severity":"MIN","claim":"CheckWaiverResponse carries no machine-readable advisory marker; active_waivers field names (rule_id, scope, approved_by, expires_at) structurally resemble an authorization grant and create a pathway for adopter hooks to misuse the response as a federation-gate bypass.","evidence":"tools.py:131–134 CheckWaiverResponse: active_waivers: list[WaiverMatch]. tools.py:94–101 WaiverMatch fields: rule_id, scope, reason, approved_by, expires_at — structurally read as an authorization record. ToolModel / SchemaVersionedResponse carry no is_advisory=True marker. An adopter hook implementing 'if check_waiver(rule_id).active_waivers: skip_rego_gate()' would silently bypass Rego enforcement, violating WP-SCP-021 §2 invariant 5. ProposeResponse.adjudication_status='queued_no_adjudicator' is the only existing response field conveying non-authoritative status; no equivalent exists on CheckWaiverResponse. Carry-forward from R1 SR-SAFE-006 (MIN, not yet applied).","impact":"Naive adopter hooks could implement waiver-check-as-gate-bypass, undermining the primary governance invariant. Risk grows proportionally with the adopter base as 021F deploys the federation hook to external repos.","mitigation":"Add is_advisory: Literal[True] = True to SchemaVersionedResponse so every response carries a machine-readable advisory marker. Add a note field to CheckWaiverResponse with the fixed string 'Active waivers do not bypass the Rego federation gate (WP-SCP-021 §2)'. Document the advisory-only contract in mcp-error-codes.md.","lens":"safety_bypass"},{"id":"SB-010","severity":"nit","claim":"Error messages embed raw exception strings and internal filesystem paths, disclosing absolute server paths to MCP clients on error conditions.","evidence":"tools.py:629: _error('SCP-MCP-E021', f'unable to read waivers: {error}') — OSError.str() includes the full waivers_path. tools.py:677: _error('SCP-MCP-E021', f'unable to parse decision log: {error}'). tools.py:690: _error('SCP-MCP-E022', f\"finding '...' was not found under {findings_dir}\") — explicitly embeds the findings_dir Path object, exposing project_root()/output/ layout. cli.py:57: FileExistsError message includes the symlink target path verbatim. Carry-forward from R1 SR-SAFE-009 (nit, not yet applied).","impact":"Server filesystem layout (absolute paths to output/findings/, project_root()) is disclosed to any MCP client that triggers an error condition. Provides path enumeration useful for local-file attack staging.","mitigation":"Log the full exception via TOOL_LOGGER.exception() server-side and replace client-facing messages with safe fixed strings ('waivers data source unavailable', 'finding not found'). Remove findings_dir from the SCP-MCP-E022 message.","lens":"safety_bypass"},{"id":"SB-011","severity":"nit","claim":"_generate_keypair reads existing key bytes for rollback using Path.read_bytes() without O_NOFOLLOW; a TOCTOU race between _refuse_symlink_target and read_bytes() can cause the server to read an attacker-controlled symlink target.","evidence":"cli.py:105: _refuse_symlink_target(out_path) calls path.is_symlink(). cli.py:115: previous_private_payload = out_path.read_bytes() if force and out_path.exists() else None. Between the is_symlink() check and read_bytes(), an attacker with write access to the key directory can atomically replace out_path with a symlink via rename(). read_bytes() then follows the symlink and reads the target's contents into memory. _write_bytes correctly uses O_NOFOLLOW (cli.py:51) for the write path; only the rollback read is unprotected.","impact":"An attacker with write access to the key directory (the same privilege required to create key files) can cause the server to read an arbitrary file into memory. If the target is a named pipe or /dev/urandom, the read may block. No data is written to the symlink target. Impact limited to the force=True key rotation path.","mitigation":"Use os.open(str(out_path), os.O_RDONLY | getattr(os, 'O_NOFOLLOW', 0)) wrapped in os.fdopen() instead of Path.read_bytes() for the rollback capture. Handle ELOOP (errno 40) as 'no previous payload' and raise FileExistsError consistent with the _write_bytes pattern.","lens":"safety_bypass"},{"id":"SB-PASS-001","severity":"nit","claim":"PASS — ToolModel.extra='forbid' confirmed on all request and response models; R1 SR-SAFE-010 finding is correctly resolved.","evidence":"tools.py:53–56: class ToolModel(BaseModel): model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid'). All 22 request/response models inherit directly from ToolModel or SchemaVersionedResponse(ToolModel). No model bypasses this configuration via a local model_config override. Verified by exhaustive class-hierarchy inspection.","impact":"None — implementation is correct.","mitigation":"No action required. Record as confirmed PASS against the extra='forbid' AC for R2.","lens":"safety_bypass"},{"id":"SB-PASS-002","severity":"nit","claim":"PASS — R1 COR-001 (stale-ref cache key) correctly resolved; _resolve_git_commit canonicalises symbolic refs to SHA before cache keying.","evidence":"tools.py:744–753: resolved_base_ref and resolved_head_ref are obtained via _resolve_git_commit (which calls git rev-parse --verify <ref>^{commit}) before _audit_cache_key is computed at line 760. Cache key = sha256(resolved_base_sha + NUL + resolved_head_sha). The test at test_audit_changed.py:9–50 exercises this path: advancing HEAD to a new SHA causes a cache miss and a second CLI call. Correctly prevents stale audit results for advancing symbolic refs.","impact":"None — implementation is correct.","mitigation":"No action required. Record as confirmed PASS against the resolved-ref cache-key AC for R2.","lens":"safety_bypass"},{"id":"SB-PASS-003","severity":"nit","claim":"PASS — R1 SR-SAFE-001 (propose race condition) correctly resolved; _proposal_creation_guard holds both threading.Lock and fcntl.flock over the entire critical section from hash check through file write.","evidence":"tools.py:541–551: _proposal_creation_guard acquires _PROPOSAL_LOCK (threading.Lock) then fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX) on lock_path; yields to the caller; releases both on exit. tools.py:822–865: the entire sequence — _existing_proposal_hashes(), _next_proposal_id(), _create_proposal_branch(), _write_new_proposal_file() — executes inside the with _proposal_creation_guard() block. _write_new_proposal_file uses O_CREAT|O_EXCL (line 568) as a final atomic guard. test_propose.py:135–197 exercises concurrent identical and concurrent distinct submissions via threading.Barrier. Correctly serialises within a process via _PROPOSAL_LOCK and across processes via flock.","impact":"None — implementation is correct.","mitigation":"No action required. Record as confirmed PASS against the propose serialisation AC for R2.","lens":"safety_bypass"}]}

findings.claim: Bidi control characters U+202A–U+202F and other Unicode Format (Cf) category characters survive NFKC normalisation and are absent from _PROPOSAL_NORMALISATION_PATTERN, leaving a residual duplicate-gate bypass after the SR-SAFE-002 R1 fix.
findings.evidence: tools.py:48: _PROPOSAL_NORMALISATION_PATTERN = re.compile(r'[\s\u200b-\u200f\u2028\u2029\ufeff]+', re.UNICODE). The range \u200b–\u200f covers U+200B–U+200F only; U+202A LEFT-TO-RIGHT EMBEDDING through U+202F RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE are not in this range. In Python re with re.UNICODE, \s matches only characters with Unicode property White_Space=True; bidi controls (U+202A–U+202F) and U+00AD SOFT HYPHEN, U+2060 WORD JOINER, U+2061–U+2064 invisible operators are category Cf (Format) and do NOT have White_Space=True. tools.py:509: unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', ...) leaves all Cf characters unchanged (no compatibility decomposition). Result: 'Add MCP policy' and 'Add\u202eMCP policy' produce distinct SHA-256 hashes after normalise→casefold→sub. test_propose.py:94–117 covers U+2028 (in pattern ✓) and U+200E (in pattern ✓) but never tests U+202E, U+00AD, or U+2060.
findings.impact: The SCP-MCP-E020 anti-spam gate is bypassed by inserting any of ~20 Format category characters invisible in UI rendering. A hostile caller can flood proposals_root with visually-identical proposals and consume PROP-NNN namespace and git branch namespace indefinitely. The R1 SR-SAFE-002 mitigation is present but incomplete; the residual bypass was introduced by choosing an explicit Unicode range rather than a category-based strip.
findings.mitigation: Replace the explicit range with a Unicode Cf/Cc category sweep: after NFKC+casefold, apply re.sub(r'[\s\u00ad\u200b-\u200f\u202a-\u202f\u2060-\u2064\u206a-\u206f\ufeff\ufff9-\ufffb]+', ' ', text), or iterate characters and drop any whose unicodedata.category() is in ('Cf','Cc','Cs'). Add test cases asserting that proposals containing U+202E (RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE), U+00AD (SOFT HYPHEN), and U+2060 (WORD JOINER) are rejected as duplicates of their clean equivalents.

findings.claim: _AUDIT_CHANGED_CACHE is accessed via a non-atomic get→TTL-check→move_to_end sequence with no mutex; concurrent threads can evict a cache entry between the get() and move_to_end() calls, causing OrderedDict.move_to_end to raise KeyError that propagates as an unhandled exception and breaks the structured-error contract.
findings.evidence: tools.py:760–763: cached = _AUDIT_CHANGED_CACHE.get(cache_key); if cached is not None and cached[0] > current_time: _AUDIT_CHANGED_CACHE.move_to_end(cache_key). There is no lock protecting this three-step sequence. Concurrently, a second thread executing audit_changed_impl reaches the write path at lines 803–806: _AUDIT_CHANGED_CACHE[cache_key2] = (...); move_to_end(cache_key2); _prune_audit_changed_cache(current_time=time.time(), max_entries=cache_max_entries). If the cache is at max capacity, _prune_audit_changed_cache calls popitem(last=False) (line 461) removing the leftmost (oldest) entry. If Thread A's cache_key is currently the oldest entry, it is evicted; Thread A then calls move_to_end(cache_key) on a now-missing key. Python's OrderedDict.move_to_end() raises KeyError on a missing key (CPython implementation). No try/except guards lines 762–763. FastMCP registers all tools as sync functions; under asyncio these run in a ThreadPoolExecutor, enabling concurrent tool calls even on stdio transport.
findings.impact: A concurrent audit_changed cache hit followed by concurrent capacity eviction raises unhandled KeyError from audit_changed_impl, surfacing as an internal exception instead of a structured SCP-MCP-E021 ErrorResponse. Violates the structured-error invariant. More likely under HTTP transport (021H) where concurrent calls are the baseline.
findings.mitigation: Protect the entire compound cache operation with a threading.Lock: acquire before get() and release after move_to_end() on hit; acquire before write and release after the post-write prune. Alternatively, wrap the move_to_end call in a try/except KeyError that treats the race as a cache miss (the safe degraded path). A third option: replace the manual OrderedDict with functools.lru_cache or cachetools.LRUCache which provide thread-safe compound operations internally.

findings.claim: propose_impl creates the git branch before writing the proposal file with no rollback; a crash or SIGKILL between _create_proposal_branch and _write_new_proposal_file burns the PROP-NNN ID permanently, causing all subsequent propose() calls to fail with 'unable to create proposal branch' and requiring manual git branch deletion to recover.
findings.evidence: tools.py:852–857: _create_proposal_branch executes git checkout -b scp-mcp-proposal/prop-NNN (via _run_git_command at tools.py:559–563), then _write_new_proposal_file is called. If the process is SIGKILL'd after branch creation but before file write, PROP-NNN.md is never written. On the next propose() call: _next_proposal_id() (lines 518–525) scans PROP-*.md via glob → finds no PROP-NNN.md → returns the same ID → _create_proposal_branch attempts git checkout -b on the already-existing branch → git returns non-zero → RuntimeError → SCP-MCP-E021. No cleanup of the orphaned branch occurs. The same stuck state arises from a non-crash failure: if _write_new_proposal_file raises OSError (disk full), the branch exists but no file is written; the identical failure loop follows. test_propose.py:48–65 tests branch-failure → no-file, but has no test for file-failure → orphaned-branch recovery.
findings.impact: Persistent DoS of the proposal tool. All subsequent propose() calls fail regardless of content. Recovery requires the server operator to manually run git branch -D scp-mcp-proposal/prop-NNN. A hostile MCP client that can induce a process crash between the two operations can permanently disable proposal submission without triggering any error visible to the operator until the next call.
findings.mitigation: Swap operation order: write the proposal file atomically first (O_CREAT|O_EXCL is the atomic anchor), then create the branch. If branch creation fails, unlink the newly-written file as cleanup. This preserves the O_EXCL atomic guarantee for the ID while making branch creation the fallible tail. Alternatively, inside the critical section after _next_proposal_id, check whether the branch name already exists (git branch --list branch_name) and skip to the next ID if the branch exists without a corresponding file.

findings.claim: The proposal lock file is opened with Path.open('a+') which follows symlinks; an attacker who can write to proposals_root before the server creates it can plant a symlink at .proposal.lock, redirecting the flock onto an arbitrary file and stalling all proposal operations indefinitely.
findings.evidence: tools.py:544: lock_path = proposals_root / '.proposal.lock'. tools.py:546: with lock_path.open('a+', encoding='utf-8') as handle. Python's Path.open() calls the libc open() with no O_NOFOLLOW flag. If an attacker creates .proposal.lock as a symlink to a file they control and hold via flock(LOCK_EX), the server's flock(LOCK_EX) call at line 547 blocks without LOCK_NB. _PROPOSAL_LOCK (line 545) is held while the flock blocks, stalling all threads in the process that call propose(). Contrast with cli.py:51 which explicitly ORs in getattr(os, 'O_NOFOLLOW', 0) for key material writes. _write_new_proposal_file correctly uses O_CREAT|O_EXCL (line 568) which refuses symlinks atomically on POSIX; the lock file has no equivalent protection.
findings.impact: Targeted DoS of the entire proposal pathway via lock-file symlink substitution. No file data is written to the lock file, so no corruption occurs; the impact is blocking. Requires write access to the proposals_root parent directory before server first-use.
findings.mitigation: Open the lock file with O_NOFOLLOW: replace lock_path.open('a+', ...) with os.fdopen(os.open(str(lock_path), os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | getattr(os, 'O_NOFOLLOW', 0), 0o600), 'r+') to match the pattern used in cli.py. Alternatively, call _refuse_symlink_target(lock_path) immediately before the open() call as a defence-in-depth check, accepting the narrow TOCTOU window.

findings.claim: AuditChangedRequest accepts unconstrained base_ref and head_ref strings; git-specific object notation (:/pattern, HEAD:path, ^{tree}, @{-N}, --upload-pack=...) can trigger unintended git operations through the subprocess calls in _list_changed_files_with_timeout and _run_audit_changed_cli.
findings.evidence: tools.py:161–163 AuditChangedRequest: base_ref: str | None = None, head_ref: str | None = None — no length cap, no character allowlist. tools.py:737–738: values are only .strip()ped then passed directly as positional argv to git diff --name-only (lines 423–429) and as --base-ref / --head-ref CLI flags (lines 476–481). Shell injection is prevented (list-form subprocess). However, git notation :/rm.*-rf triggers a commit-message regex scan across the full reflog; HEAD:path/to/blob reads a blob object from the tree; refs/heads/../../evil attempts path traversal in the ref namespace. A ref string beginning with -- (e.g., --upload-pack=/path/to/script) would be passed as a git option flag to the git diff invocation. Carry-forward from R1 SR-SAFE-005 (MIN, not yet applied in current code).
findings.impact: Unexpected git operations: reflog regex evaluation, blob reads, potential remote-tracking ref fetches. A --upload-pack= prefix could invoke an attacker-controlled script on systems where git network operations are available. CPU and subprocess resource amplification per call. More exploitable under HTTP transport (021H).
findings.mitigation: Validate base_ref and head_ref with a restrictive allowlist before use: re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z0-9_.~^@{}:/\-]{1,200}', ref) with explicit rejection of strings starting with - (to prevent option injection). Return SCP-MCP-E021 for invalid refs. Document the allowed syntax in mcp-error-codes.md under SCP-MCP-E021.

findings.claim: resolve_domain_impl silently normalises path traversal sequences in changed_files without rejecting them; confidence=0.0 / empty-domains output for traversal inputs provides a pathway for fail-open adopter hooks to skip the consult gate.
findings.evidence: tools.py:173–174 ResolveDomainRequest: changed_files: list[str] — no element validator. tools.py:379: normalised = changed_file.replace('\\', '/').strip('/') — strip('/') removes leading slashes but not ../ sequences. The input '../../etc/passwd' normalises to '../../etc/passwd' and is passed to exact_map.get() (no match) and _fuzzy_domains_for_path() (no heuristic match) → empty domains, confidence=0.0. No filesystem operations occur on user-supplied paths; direct traversal exploitation is not possible in the current code path. Carry-forward from R1 SR-SAFE-004 (MIN, not yet applied).
findings.impact: An adopter hook implementing fail-open logic on confidence=0.0 or empty-domains would skip the consult requirement for a changed_files list that includes traversal-containing entries. This is the 021F N-3 failure mode (b) pathway: domain-resolver confusion silently opens the consult gate.
findings.mitigation: Add a validator on ResolveDomainRequest.changed_files elements: reject any path element matching re.search(r'(?:^|/)\.\.(?:/|$)', p) and return SCP-MCP-E021. Add a test asserting that traversal-containing inputs return SCP-MCP-E021 rather than empty-domains/confidence-0.0.

findings.claim: CheckFindingResponse.finding and AuditChangedResponse.audit_result are typed dict[str, Any]; ToolModel extra='forbid' does not restrict the contents of these opaque dicts, so any field added to findings JSON or audit CLI output is immediately disclosed to all MCP clients without a schema gate.
findings.evidence: tools.py:158: CheckFindingResponse.finding: dict[str, Any]. tools.py:170: AuditChangedResponse.audit_result: dict[str, Any]. tools.py:686: return CheckFindingResponse(finding=finding) where finding is the entire on-disk JSON object returned verbatim by _extract_finding_objects(). ToolModel.model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid') (line 56) rejects extra top-level Pydantic fields but does not inspect the contents of dict[str, Any] typed fields. Future additions to finding objects (e.g., pre_disclosure_notes, cve_ids, internal_contact) would be immediately accessible via check_finding without any schema change. Carry-forward from R1 SR-SAFE-007 (MIN, not yet applied).
findings.impact: Information disclosure: sensitive fields added to findings JSON or audit CLI output are exposed to all MCP clients. Blast radius grows as the adopter base expands in 021F and WP-SCP-024.
findings.mitigation: Define a typed FindingCard Pydantic model (finding_id, rule_id, domain, severity, summary, status, area_id) and use it as the type for CheckFindingResponse.finding. Validate through FindingCard.model_validate() to strip unexpected fields. Apply a parallel allowlist model for AuditChangedResponse.audit_result.

findings.claim: subprocess.run() in _run_audit_changed_cli kills only the direct child on TimeoutExpired; grandchild git subprocesses spawned by the audit CLI are orphaned, accumulating file descriptors and memory under repeated timeout conditions.
findings.evidence: tools.py:487–494: subprocess.run(command, cwd=project_root(), ..., timeout=timeout_seconds) with no start_new_session=True or preexec_fn=os.setsid. On TimeoutExpired CPython sends SIGKILL to the direct child (the audit-changed CLI) but does not propagate to its process group. The audit CLI in turn invokes git diff, git log, etc. (itself calls _run_git_command); those grandchildren continue after their parent is killed. Carry-forward from R1 SR-SAFE-008 (MIN, not yet applied).
findings.impact: Under repeated or sustained timeout conditions, orphaned git processes accumulate file descriptors and address space. In a long-lived HTTP transport (021H) server, sustained flooding of audit_changed with slow refs can exhaust OS process table entries and file descriptor limits, degrading or crashing the host process.
findings.mitigation: Replace subprocess.run() with subprocess.Popen(start_new_session=True), capture proc.pid, and on TimeoutExpired call os.killpg(os.getpgid(proc.pid), signal.SIGKILL) to reap the full process group. Wrap communicate() in a try/finally for the killpg path.

findings.claim: CheckWaiverResponse carries no machine-readable advisory marker; active_waivers field names (rule_id, scope, approved_by, expires_at) structurally resemble an authorization grant and create a pathway for adopter hooks to misuse the response as a federation-gate bypass.
findings.evidence: tools.py:131–134 CheckWaiverResponse: active_waivers: list[WaiverMatch]. tools.py:94–101 WaiverMatch fields: rule_id, scope, reason, approved_by, expires_at — structurally read as an authorization record. ToolModel / SchemaVersionedResponse carry no is_advisory=True marker. An adopter hook implementing 'if check_waiver(rule_id).active_waivers: skip_rego_gate()' would silently bypass Rego enforcement, violating WP-SCP-021 §2 invariant 5. ProposeResponse.adjudication_status='queued_no_adjudicator' is the only existing response field conveying non-authoritative status; no equivalent exists on CheckWaiverResponse. Carry-forward from R1 SR-SAFE-006 (MIN, not yet applied).
findings.impact: Naive adopter hooks could implement waiver-check-as-gate-bypass, undermining the primary governance invariant. Risk grows proportionally with the adopter base as 021F deploys the federation hook to external repos.
findings.mitigation: Add is_advisory: Literal[True] = True to SchemaVersionedResponse so every response carries a machine-readable advisory marker. Add a note field to CheckWaiverResponse with the fixed string 'Active waivers do not bypass the Rego federation gate (WP-SCP-021 §2)'. Document the advisory-only contract in mcp-error-codes.md.

findings.claim: Error messages embed raw exception strings and internal filesystem paths, disclosing absolute server paths to MCP clients on error conditions.
findings.evidence: tools.py:629: _error('SCP-MCP-E021', f'unable to read waivers: {error}') — OSError.str() includes the full waivers_path. tools.py:677: _error('SCP-MCP-E021', f'unable to parse decision log: {error}'). tools.py:690: _error('SCP-MCP-E022', f"finding '...' was not found under {findings_dir}") — explicitly embeds the findings_dir Path object, exposing project_root()/output/ layout. cli.py:57: FileExistsError message includes the symlink target path verbatim. Carry-forward from R1 SR-SAFE-009 (nit, not yet applied).
findings.impact: Server filesystem layout (absolute paths to output/findings/, project_root()) is disclosed to any MCP client that triggers an error condition. Provides path enumeration useful for local-file attack staging.
findings.mitigation: Log the full exception via TOOL_LOGGER.exception() server-side and replace client-facing messages with safe fixed strings ('waivers data source unavailable', 'finding not found'). Remove findings_dir from the SCP-MCP-E022 message.

findings.claim: _generate_keypair reads existing key bytes for rollback using Path.read_bytes() without O_NOFOLLOW; a TOCTOU race between _refuse_symlink_target and read_bytes() can cause the server to read an attacker-controlled symlink target.
findings.evidence: cli.py:105: _refuse_symlink_target(out_path) calls path.is_symlink(). cli.py:115: previous_private_payload = out_path.read_bytes() if force and out_path.exists() else None. Between the is_symlink() check and read_bytes(), an attacker with write access to the key directory can atomically replace out_path with a symlink via rename(). read_bytes() then follows the symlink and reads the target's contents into memory. _write_bytes correctly uses O_NOFOLLOW (cli.py:51) for the write path; only the rollback read is unprotected.
findings.impact: An attacker with write access to the key directory (the same privilege required to create key files) can cause the server to read an arbitrary file into memory. If the target is a named pipe or /dev/urandom, the read may block. No data is written to the symlink target. Impact limited to the force=True key rotation path.
findings.mitigation: Use os.open(str(out_path), os.O_RDONLY | getattr(os, 'O_NOFOLLOW', 0)) wrapped in os.fdopen() instead of Path.read_bytes() for the rollback capture. Handle ELOOP (errno 40) as 'no previous payload' and raise FileExistsError consistent with the _write_bytes pattern.
